acceptance: On timeout, adapters that can do so cancel the statement and stop the session this run started, shown with stubbed clients.
A warning tells cloud users that remote work may continue and that cleanup is not live-verified.
The per-adapter capability table is in the pull request.
description:
## Problem
When BenchBox stops at a timeout, a query, job or session it started on a remote platform can keep running and billing.

## Owner decision
"build the remote cleanup, verify it with stubbed clients only, and print a warning on cloud platforms that remote work may continue after a timeout until a live check has been done. No live cloud runs." Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
First list every adapter under benchbox/platforms that starts remote work and what its client offers to cancel a statement and to stop a session, job or cluster BenchBox itself started; put the table in the pull request. Add one adapter hook the timeout path calls, implemented where the client supports it. Only stop what this run started; never stop a warehouse, cluster or session that existed before the run. For every cloud platform, print the warning when `--timeout` is set, naming whether cleanup is implemented for that platform. Adapter SDK imports stay lazy.

## Decision gates
No live cloud run, no credentials used. Verification is by stubbed clients, and the docs and the warning say cleanup has not been checked against live services. If an adapter cannot tell what it started from what pre-existed, it implements no cleanup and the table says so. The warning's wording is shown in the pull request body.

## Verification rubric
Pass: per adapter with cleanup, a test with a stubbed client shows the cancel and stop calls are made on timeout for resources the run started and not for pre-existing ones; a test shows the hook is called from the timeout path and that a failing cleanup does not hide the timeout (exit code stays 124, the cleanup error is reported); the warning appears for cloud platforms when `--timeout` is set and not otherwise; `make platform-manifest-check` and `make pr-preflight` exit 0.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text the owner has not already chosen is shown to the owner before it is committed. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
